item.content:encoded:
Ok, here we go.

Dancer enters stage right

Begins in a serious manor, making large steps and quizzical gestures. Slowly the dancer's demeanor becomes for jovial, until they are skipping around and blowing raspberries at the audience. This symbolizes the comedic nature of the piece in contrast to the normal clinical tone.

Dancer exits stage.

A new dancer enters, and one other enters on rafters above.

The dancer above acts in a authoritative yet casual manner while the one below is worried by some object unseen by the audience.

Above dancer performs some morderatally complex motions, with the below dancer attempting to follow suite, with less skill.

This continues until the above dancer abruptly leaves.

Below dancer is becoming progressively more worried, trying to do what above dancer was doing, until finally being chased off the stage by something unseen.

FIN.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I don't really know how to feel about this. For one, it doesn't strike me as a -J - it seems like the doctor or someone could easily have just needed something to write instructions on so it grabbed this off the top of some forms. The idea is nice, and I like the way it's written, particularly how it's not so serious as to lose the attractive lighthearted tone, nor so whacky as to lose any sense of setting or tone. I feel compelled to upvote mostly because I just haven't read anything like this on the wiki before; it's refreshingly unique and for that reason alone I approve of it very heartily. Should you decide to remove and/or rework this I would, tenatively, recommend getting rid of that ambiguity and work on making this a strictly formal work set in a period where anomalous pets are taboo and regulated heavily but not necessarily illegal, or on the flipside just get rid of the pretenses and focus on the laughs, which I found to be distinctly lacking as a rule of thumb.

item.title: Author's Post
item.content:encoded:
This has been sitting in my sandbox for about a year or so, with divided opinions from the people I sought critique from, none of whom had anything too solid to give me. After a year of not being able to figure out what to do with it, I figured I should just post it and see what happens.

Thanks to the people who critiqued this, whom I've certainly forgotten the names of.
